nameStory: The scrawled filefish gets its name from the intricate, seemingly random lines and scribbles that decorate its body, looking like someone took a pen and doodled all over it. The 'filefish' part comes from their rough, sandpaper-like skin that feels like it could file wood smooth. Some folks call it the broomtail filefish because its tail fin can spread out wide like the bristles of a broom.
description: The scrawled filefish is a truly unusual-looking ocean wanderer that's shaped like a flattened oval with a long, narrow tail. Its most striking feature is the maze of blue lines and scribbles that cover its brownish body, making each fish look like a unique piece of underwater art. These medium-sized fish can grow quite large, and their bodies feel surprisingly rough and leathery to the touch. They're tropical visitors that only rarely venture into New England waters, making any sighting a special event.

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Distinctive blue scribbled lines and patterns cover a tan to brownish background, like someone drew all over the fish with a blue marker

idTips.label: Body Shape
idTips.description: Compressed, oval-shaped body that's taller than it is thick, with a distinctly narrow tail section

idTips.label: Fins
idTips.description: Single prominent dorsal spine that can be raised or lowered, and a fan-like tail fin that can spread wide

idTips.label: Texture
idTips.description: Skin feels rough and sandpaper-like, with tiny scales that give it a leathery texture

idTips.label: Mouth
idTips.description: Small terminal mouth at the front tip of a slightly pointed snout, designed for picking at small prey

habitat: In New England waters, scrawled filefish are extremely rare visitors typically found in offshore areas during unusually warm years when tropical currents bring them north. When present, they prefer areas around floating seaweed, offshore structures, or the open ocean where they can drift with currents. They're usually found in warmer surface waters rather than near the bottom.

seasonality.spring: Extremely unlikely to be seen, as water temperatures are still too cold for these tropical visitors.
seasonality.summer: The only season when scrawled filefish might appear in New England, during exceptionally warm years when tropical waters extend unusually far north.
seasonality.fall: Possible but rare sightings early in the season if warm water masses linger, but they'll disappear as temperatures drop.
seasonality.winter: Never present in New England waters during winter months due to cold temperatures.

funFact: Scrawled filefish are like underwater chameleons - they can dramatically change their color and pattern in seconds to blend with their surroundings, and those blue scribbles can fade to nearly invisible or become bold and bright depending on their mood and environment!
confusionNotes: The intricate blue scribbled pattern makes scrawled filefish nearly impossible to confuse with any other New England fish - no other species has anything close to this distinctive 'drawn-on' appearance.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called a 'filefish,' this species is completely unrelated to any freshwater fish and belongs to the same group as pufferfish and triggerfish, which explains their unusual body shape and swimming style.
compareHints: Scrawled filefish are much larger and more distinctively patterned than their cousin the orange filefish, which is smaller and lacks the characteristic blue scribbles. While orange filefish are more commonly seen in New England (though still rare), scrawled filefish are unmistakable due to their size and intricate line patterns. Both share the rough, file-like skin texture that gives the family its name.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Orange filefish can be distinguished from its relatives, the dotterel filefish and scrawled filefish, by its solid orange coloration and smaller size.
Unlike its Orange Filefish relative which has bright orange coloration, or the Scrawled Filefish with its distinctive blue scribbly markings, the Dotterel Filefish is relatively plain in coloration.
